title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the digression (from the previous page) on 'germes d'espaces'. A germ of space is a pair (S, 𝔏): a space S with a filter 𝔏 of subsets, typically the neighbourhoods of a subset Y, possibly restricted to X∖Y.

The local situation Grothendieck has in mind is a point x of a space X with a neighbourhood homeomorphic to ℝ², i.e. X is a surface at x. He writes D_{X,x} (or D_x) for the germ of X at x, which is trivially 1-connected. He writes D*_{X,x} (or D*_x) for the residual germ, i.e. the germ of the punctured disc. He wants to choose a universal covering D*~_x of D*_x. To make sense of this he digresses on what a universal covering of an abstract germ of space is.

The definition goes as follows.
- A covering of a germ 𝔖=(S,𝔏) is represented by a covering S'_i → S_i of some member S_i ∈ 𝔏. So Rev(𝔖) is the 2-colimit of Rev(S_i) over S_i ∈ 𝔏.
- Such a covering defines a germ (S'_i, 𝔏_{S'_i}), where 𝔏_{S'_i} is the inverse image of the induced filter.
- Up to unique isomorphism of germs over 𝔖, this germ depends only on the class in Rev(𝔖), not on the representatives S_i, S'_i.
- Hence there is a canonical functor Rev(𝔖) → (Germes)/𝔖. The next page, (54), asserts it is fully faithful and defines étale coverings of a germ as its essential image.

The purpose comes from (51), the next page and the margin. Where Rev(𝔖) is multigalois, its 1-connected objects (universal coverings) are themselves germs. Then π₁(𝔖, 𝔖~) ≅ Aut(𝔖~), which recovers the abstract Galois-category π₁.

For the punctured-disc germ, the universal cover is (up to homeomorphism) the germ at infinity of a half-plane, with automorphism group ℤ. Choosing it amounts to a 'base point at the puncture'. This gives canonical local inertia subgroups (with a generator fixed by orientation) inside the fundamental group of a surface with punctures. These are the ingredients of the Longue Marche / Teichmüller-tower setting: decomposition and inertia at points and boundary components, without a choice of ordinary base point.
errors: No mathematical errors. A small gap: full faithfulness of Rev(𝔖) → Germes/𝔖 (asserted on the next page) depends on morphisms of germs being germs of maps defined on some member of the filter. This is implicit, not stated.

ideas.what: Germs of spaces as pairs (space, filter); residual germ of X at a point (the punctured neighbourhood germ)
ideas.modern_name: pro-spaces / germs at a subspace; the link of a point viewed as a pro-object
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (shape theory, pro-objects: Grothendieck SGA4, Artin–Mazur)
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (circulated 1981) treats related local-at-points constructions; unsure about this exact formalism

ideas.what: Category of coverings of a germ as a colimit of Rev(S_i), realized as a full subcategory of germs over the germ (étale coverings of a germ)
ideas.modern_name: covering theory of pro-spaces / fundamental group of a germ (local fundamental group at infinity)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; local fundamental groups (SGA2 for the algebraic analogue)
ideas.where_published: algebraic analogue in SGA1/SGA2 (local π₁, Galois categories)

ideas.what: Choice of a universal covering of the punctured disc germ at a surface point, to define a canonical inertia group without a base point
ideas.modern_name: tangential base points / canonical inertia generators at punctures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points'); Ihara, Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche discuss inertia at punctures; tangential base points in this form are not explicit there to my knowledge

missed.claim: A topological precursor of tangential base points: a 'base point at a puncture' is defined as a universal covering of the residual germ (punctured-disc germ) at a point of a surface.
missed.quote: Je m'intéresse au choix d'un revêtement universel D*~ de D*
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This documents that Grothendieck formalized base-point-free inertia at punctures via germs of coverings in the Longue Marche period, independently of and probably before Deligne's tangential base points. The idea itself is now standard, so this is historical interest rather than new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful foundational setup of coverings of germs, aimed at canonical inertia at punctures. Mathematically routine, and the idea is now standard in the form of tangential base points. Mild historical interest only.
transcription_corrections: 'groupe résiduel de X en π (contenu dans le groupe D_{x,π} ...)' should read 'germe résiduel de X en x (contenu dans le germe D_{X,x} ou D_x de X en x)'.
'ici X est un revêtement[?] en x' should read 'ici X est une surface en x'.
'pour ce qu'il me faut' should read roughly 'mais pour ceci il me faut faire une digression sur la notion abstraite de revêtement universel d'un germe d'espace'.
'à isomorphisme unique près de groupes' should read '... près de germes'.
